nodes.statement: The product is currently defined as 'secretome retaining EVs' versus a purified small‑EV drug substance; this distinction is unresolved and blocks product definition and CMC decisions.

If a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (intact-EV capture, particle counts, detergent/protease sensitivity, density correlation) is observed, then the preparation can be classified as an EV-enriched small‑EV preparation rather than mainly non‑vesicular secretome.

If no membrane-protected, particle-associated signature is observed and marker signal tracks with bulk soluble protein and is insensitive to membrane disruption, then the preparation is indistinguishable from an unpurified secretome with co-isolated non‑vesicular components.
Classifying the drug‑substance fractionation state enables targeted CMC actions: orthogonal QC panel, potency assay development, and relevant scale-up comparability testing (MISEV2023 guidance).

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Which measurable composition distinction can discriminate a secretome-retaining-EV product from a small-EV preparation?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow combining: (1) density-gradient fractionation followed by particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact material per fraction; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched preparations: (A) enriched small-EV preparation vs (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining EVs) from the same source-cell lot.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative control: buffer-only and detergent-disrupted samples; Positive control: commercially available characterized small EVs if available.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned medium lots (same passage/bank)
Access to validated capture reagents and particle counting instrumentation
Laboratory capability for density fractionation
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No qualitative difference between enriched small-EV preparation and secretome control in co-localization of capture signal with particle peaks, or lack of membrane-protection behavior (i.e., captured signal unaffected by detergent/protease/RNase) indicating inability to discriminate fractionation state.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If the criteria for success are not met across independent replicates, the hypothesis is falsified and the program must treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome with respect to intact-EV identity and re-evaluate fractionation strategy.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: A membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (immuno-capture of EV surface markers + particle enumeration + detergent/protease protection + density fractionation) will be observed in a purified small-EV preparation but not in an unpurified concentrated secretome.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment (indicating membrane protection).

nodes.statement: A discrete, membrane-protected cargo population associated with intact EVs exists in MSC-conditioned medium and can be recovered in particle-containing density fractions.
The membrane-protected, particle-associated fraction carries a reproducible neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity measurable in a standardized in vitro assay.

Membrane disruption (detergent + protease/RNase) abolishes the bioactivity if it is EV-membrane-protected; non-EV soluble co-isolates will show bioactivity that is detergent/protease-insensitive and will not co-localize with particle peaks.
If n1-n3 are observed reproducibly across source-cell lots, this attribute can be used as a candidate potency-linked product-identity metric to guide fractionation and CMC decisions.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Does a membrane-protected, intact-EV-associated fraction from MSC-conditioned medium carry the measurable neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity (in vitro) that is absent from non-EV secretome fractions after matched fractionation?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow: (1) density-gradient fractionation with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture of intact EV markers on fractions; (3) protease/RNase protection +/- detergent on capture material; (4) in vitro neuroinflammation-modulation assay applied to matched fractions or eluates; (5) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched preparations from the same conditioned-medium lots: (A) enriched small-EV preparation vs (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only fractions, detergent-disrupted fractions; Positive controls: purified characterized small EVs and recombinant positive control modulators of the assay (e.g., dexamethasone or known anti-inflammatory agent) to verify assay responsiveness.

minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible co-localization of bioactivity with particle-count/capture-positive fractions across replicates, or bioactivity in capture-positive fractions is unchanged by membrane-disrupting treatments (detergent + protease/RNase), indicating the activity is not membrane-protected/EV-associated.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If the failure criterion is met, the hypothesis is falsified and the program must treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from a secretome for potency and product-definition purposes and revisit fractionation or product strategy.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: A membrane-protected, particle-associated fraction recovered from MSC-conditioned medium will contain a reproducible neuroinflammation-modulating bioactivity (in vitro) that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is abolished by detergent + protease/RNase treatment, whereas non-EV secretome fractions will either lack this activity or show detergent-insensitive activity.

edges.uncertainty: High: existing rodent efficacy and MISEV guidance support need for orthogonal linkage, but do not demonstrate the in vivo→ex vivo bridge or that membrane protection is required for in vivo readout.

edges.competing_explanation: Failure to detect in vivo exposure could arise from assay insensitivity or labeling artifacts rather than absence of intact EVs.
edges.missing_experiment: A matched intact-EV verification assay in a relevant large-animal or rodent model concurrent with short-term ex vivo tissue sampling.

nodes.statement: An orthogonally defined intact-EV signature (capture-positive, particle-peak co-localization, detergent/protease-sensitive) identifies a membrane-protected fraction in the drug substance.

If an administered preparation contains the orthogonal intact-EV signature and intact-EV exposure in the nasal→CSF/olfactory mucosa compartment is demonstrable in vivo, then downstream CNS immune cells (microglia-like cells) will show a reproducible ex vivo modulation measurable in a standardized cytokine readout.

If the preparation lacks the intact-EV signature or the captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, then the ex vivo CNS readout will be absent or qualitatively different, showing that bulk particle counts alone do not predict the assay outcome.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Can an orthogonal in vivo-to-ex vivo bridging experiment demonstrate that an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (verified by capture + detergent protection) produces a reproducible, measurable modulation of an ex vivo CNS inflammatory readout after intranasal dosing, independent of bulk particle counts?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Integrated protocol: (A) characterize administered materials in vitro with orthogonal intact-EV workflow (density fractionation + particle counts + immuno-capture + detergent/protease protection); (B) intranasal administration to rodents with short post-dose interval (predefined, brief window) followed by collection of nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue; (C) orthogonal verification of intact-EV exposure in collected fluids/tissues (capture and particle counts); (D) prepare ex vivo tissue or isolated microglia-like cells from harvested tissue, apply standardized inflammatory challenge (e.g., LPS) and measure cytokine release with and without co-incubation with eluates from captured fractions; (E) compare cytokine responses across arms.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Four-arm comparison from the same conditioned-medium lot: (1) intact-EV-enriched preparation (capture-positive), (2) secretome-retaining concentrated conditioned medium (capture profile to be determined), (3) intact-EV-enriched material treated with detergent + protease prior to administration (membrane-disrupted), (4) particle-count-matched but capture-depleted preparation (if achievable).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Positive control: characterized small EVs and dexamethasone in the ex vivo assay. Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions. In-assay viability/assay controls for tissue health.
dependencies: Availability of sufficient conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank and passage range
Validated immuno-capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation sensitivity for low-biomass lavage/CSF samples
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval tissue/fluid collection
Laboratory capability to run both orthogonal capture and ex vivo inflammatory assays with required throughput
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible linkage between in vivo orthogonal intact-EV verification and the ex vivo cytokine readout across replicates (i.e., capture-positive verification does not predict ex vivo modulation), or particle-count-matched capture-negative or membrane-disrupted arms produce equivalent ex vivo effects, indicating activity is not intact-EV-associated.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, treat the material as functionally indistinguishable from secretome with respect to the tested short-term ex vivo inflammatory readout; revise product-definition toward secretome-centric strategy and deprioritize EV-specific potency attribute.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: An intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected fraction (verified by capture + detergent/protease sensitivity and particle-peak co-localization) is necessary for a reproducible short-term ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation following intranasal administration; particle-count-matched but capture-negative or membrane-disrupted material will not produce the same ex vivo modulation.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Magnitude and reproducibility of ex vivo cytokine modulation (e.g., reduction in LPS-induced IL-6/TNF-α) from tissue-derived microglia-like cells correlated with in vivo orthogonal evidence of intact-EV exposure (presence of capture-positive signal and particle co-localization in lavage/CSF/tissue).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Can an orthogonal in vivo→ex vivo bridging experiment show that only material with an intact-EV signature (capture-positive and detergent/protease-sensitive) produces a reproducible short-term ex vivo CNS inflammatory modulation after intranasal dosing, independent of bulk particle counts?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium from a single characterized source-cell lot processed to produce: (A) enriched small-EV preparation (SEC/UC) and (B) concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) from the same lot
Matched aliquots of capture-positive material treated with detergent + protease (membrane-disrupted) prior to administration
Particle-count instruments and reagents (NTA or TRPS)
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV surface markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Assays for orthogonal in vivo verification: capture from nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory mucosa homogenates and particle counts

Short-term ex vivo CNS inflammatory assay platform (e.g., acutely harvested rodent olfactory bulb or olfactory mucosa–adjacent tissue processed to isolate microglia-like cells, LPS challenge ex vivo, and cytokine readouts such as IL-6/TNF-α ELISA or multiplex)
Positive control materials: characterized small EVs (commercial or lab-validated) and a known anti-inflammatory control (e.g., dexamethasone) for the ex vivo assay
Negative controls: vehicle-only and buffer fractions
secondary_readouts: Co-localization metrics between particle-count peaks and capture-positive signal in administered material and in collected lavage/CSF fractions
Confirmation that captured material's activity is abolished by detergent + protease pre-treatment
Protein:particle ratios of administered materials and of captured fractions
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium preps and separate animal cohorts)
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In multiple independent conditioned-medium lots and animal cohorts (n ≥ 3), only the arm where administered material is orthogonally verified as capture-positive and shows particle-peak co-localization produces a reproducible reduction in ex vivo inflammatory cytokine readout; this reduction is abolished when captured material is membrane-disrupted prior to administration, and particle-count-matched capture-negative or secretome-retaining arms do not produce equivalent ex vivo modulation.

prior_hypotheses.proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Define a candidate potency attribute as an intact-EV-associated, membrane-protected bioactivity that (A) co-localizes with capture-positive particle fractions in source material, (B) is abolished by membrane-disrupting treatment in the captured material, and (C) is predictive of a short-term ex vivo CNS inflammatory-response modulation after intranasal administration when intact-EV exposure is orthogonally verified in vivo.

edges.uncertainty: Inference: MISEV and source-consistency notes support source-dependent composition, but do not define senescence as causal; uncertainty is moderate.

edges.competing_explanation: Lack of CNS detection in macaque could result from route, dosing, labeling sensitivity, or species-specific mucociliary clearance rather than source-cell-dependent EV integrity.
edges.missing_experiment: Matched short-interval in vivo dosing and orthogonal intact-EV verification comparing materials from early- versus late-passage MSCs.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: macaque negative biodistribution suggests delivery barriers but does not identify source-cell senescence as the cause; alternative formulation/labeling factors may explain poor detectability.

nodes.statement: Donor-MSC senescence state (operationalized by passage number and p16/p21 expression) determines features of the released particle population (membrane integrity, surface-marker display, particle:protein ratio).

These senescence-linked particle features produce a distinct orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature: capture-positive signal that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive versus marker signal that tracks with bulk soluble protein and is detergent-insensitive.

Materials with the senescence-favorable intact-EV signature are more likely to produce short-interval in vivo evidence of intact-EV presence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after intranasal dosing than materials from senescent MSC sources.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Does the donor MSC senescence state (early-passage, low p16/p21 expression versus late-passage, high p16/p21 expression) causally alter (A) the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) and (B) short-interval nasal→CSF/olfactory-mucosa intact-EV detection after matched intranasal dosing of conditioned-medium-derived preparations?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow: (1) density-gradient fractionation with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) measure total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction. For in vivo arm: perform orthogonal capture and particle count on short-interval collected lavage/CSF/tissues.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched conditioned-medium-derived preparations from the same donor source processed identically: early-passage (low p16/p21) versus late-passage (high p16/p21); within each, compare enriched small-EV preparation and secretome-retaining preparation. Include detergent/protease-disrupted aliquots as membrane-disruption controls.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only, vehicle-only, and detergent-disrupted capture material. Positive controls: commercially available characterized small EVs (if available) and a lab-validated non-senescent MSC small-EV preparation.
dependencies: Availability of matched donor MSC lots expanded to generate clear early- vs late-passage senescence marker separation
Analytical capability for orthogonal intact-EV workflow and sensitive capture from low-biomass in vivo samples
Animal protocol approvals for short-interval sample collection
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible difference between early- and late-passage source materials in orthogonal intact-EV signatures or in short-interval in vivo recoverable capture/particle evidence across biological replicates; detergent/protease sensitivity does not differ by source senescence state.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, the hypothesis that source-cell senescence state deterministically controls intact-EV analytical signature and short-interval intranasal recoverability is falsified; the program should deprioritize senescence as a gating source-cell specification and investigate alternative source or process variables (donor genetics, media, purification artifacts) as drivers of observed variability.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: Conditioned medium from early-passage, low-p16/p21 MSCs will yield an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and greater short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV evidence in nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa after matched intranasal dosing compared with conditioned medium from late-passage, high-p16/p21 MSCs.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in conditioned-medium-derived preparations; presence/absence and relative magnitude of capture-positive signal and particle counts in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing comparing early- versus late-passage source materials.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Does donor-MSC senescence state (early vs late passage as measured by p16/p21 expression) causally affect orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature in conditioned-medium-derived preparations and short-interval in vivo recoverable intact-EV signal after intranasal dosing?
required_material: MSC source matched donor(s) expanded to generate: (A) early-passage, low p16/p21 expression lots and (B) late-passage, high p16/p21 expression lots (same donor where feasible)

Conditioned medium produced from each source-cell lot processed identically into: (1) enriched small-EV preparation (SEC/UC) and (2) concentrated conditioned medium without EV enrichment (secretome-retaining)
Immuno-capture reagents for intact EV markers (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) and fractionation equipment
Protease (proteinase K), RNase reagents, and detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent)

Short-interval in vivo dosing capability and animal cohorts (rodent), with ability to collect nasal lavage, CSF (if feasible), and olfactory-mucosa/olfactory-bulb-adjacent tissue at predefined short post-dose intervals
Total protein assay reagents and orthogonal capture ELISA/reporter assays
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio differences between early- and late-passage preparations and fractions
Reproducibility across independent biological replicates (n ≥ 3 conditioned-medium lots per senescence state)
Comparative yield and stability of captured material after incubation in nasal-simulating medium (ex vivo muco-ciliary mimic) as an orthogonal stability proxy
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: Across independent biological replicates (n ≥ 3), materials from early-passage, low p16/p21 MSCs show (A) clear co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and detergent/protease-sensitive capture signal in the orthogonal workflow, and (B) detectable capture-positive signal and particle-co-localization in short-interval nasal lavage/CSF/olfactory-mucosa samples after intranasal dosing; materials from late-passage, high p16/p21 MSCs do not reproducibly show these features under identical processing and dosing conditions.

prior_hypotheses.proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, adopt a source-cell qualification attribute: donor-MSC senescence-status (operationalized by passage range and p16/p21 expression) as a determinative input to lot-definition and a required stratifier for downstream orthogonal intact-EV identity and short-interval intranasal biodistribution testing.
prior_hypotheses.title: Hypothesis: MSC source-cell senescence state controls intact-EV identity, membrane-protection, and short-interval intranasal CNS exposure potential

edges.competing_explanation: An apparent capture-positive co-localization could reflect residual non-vesicular particles (lipoproteins/aggregates) that co-elute in the chosen SEC/iodixanol window.
edges.missing_experiment: Program-specific demonstration that the proposed two-step, scalable workflow produces a membrane-protected, capture-positive particle peak distinct from secretome concentrate and with acceptable yield metrics.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV recommends orthogonal characterization and suggests fractionation state matters for identity and potency, but does not specify that a TFF→SEC→single-cushion workflow will preserve membrane-protected signatures at manufacturing yields.

edges.competing_explanation: Lack of CNS detection in macaque might be due to administration, labeling, or species clearance differences rather than fractionation state.
edges.missing_experiment: Orthogonal intact-EV verification from materials produced by the scalable workflow tested in short-interval in vivo dosing to confirm detectability in relevant compartments.
edges.uncertainty: High: large-animal negative biodistribution suggests delivery/exposure risks that make establishing a reproducible drug-substance identity even more critical for subsequent bridging studies.

nodes.statement: A scalable fractionation workflow (TFF → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) can produce a size- and density-bounded fraction with a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle-count peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity).

The concentrated conditioned-medium (secretome-retaining) processed only by TFF concentration lacks the co-localized capture-positive particle peak and shows marker signal that is largely detergent/protease-insensitive, consistent with non-vesicular co-isolates.

If n1 is true and yields are manufacturable, the bounded small-EV fraction can serve as a reproducible drug-substance definition to support orthogonal QC and potency assay development (inference; uncertainty noted).

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Can a scalable two-step fractionation (tangential-flow concentration + size-exclusion chromatography (SEC) followed by a limited iodixanol cushion that preserves yield) produce a reproducible intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease sensitivity) that is absent from a concentrated secretome and is compatible with reasonable manufacturing yield?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal workflow: (1) perform density-fractionation of the candidate fraction (single-cushion fractions) with particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease/RNase protection ± detergent on captured material; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) measure manufacturing yield metrics (mass and particle recovery) across workflows.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched preparations from the same conditioned-medium lot: (A) TFF-concentrated secretome-retaining material (no SEC/cushion) versus (B) TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol-cushion bounded small-EV fraction.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Negative controls: buffer-only, detergent-disrupted captured material. Positive control: commercially available characterized small EVs or lab-validated small-EV preparation (if available) to verify capture and particle-count co-localization behavior.
dependencies: Availability of consistent source-cell conditioned-medium lots (same passage/bank)
Access to capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Analytical capacity for single-step iodixanol cushion fractionation and rapid particle counting
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No qualitative difference between the bounded small-EV fraction and concentrated secretome in co-localization or membrane-protection behavior across replicates, or yields are consistently inadequate for manufacturing considerations.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criteria are met, the hypothesis is falsified: the proposed scalable fractionation does not produce an analytically distinct intact-EV drug-substance candidate and the program should treat the material as indistinguishable from secretome for product-definition and prioritize alternative isolation strategies or secretome-centric product definitions.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: A scalable, two-step fractionation (TFF→SEC→single-step iodixanol cushion) yields a size-and-density-bounded fraction with a membrane-protected, particle-associated analytical signature that is absent from concentrated secretome, while providing acceptable yield for manufacturing consideration.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and demonstrable loss of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in the bounded small-EV fraction but not in the concentrated secretome; plus qualitative assessment of yield (recovery sufficient to support GMP-like batch considerations).
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Can the proposed scalable fractionation workflow (TFF concentration → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) produce a bounded small-EV fraction that (A) displays an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and (B) achieves manufacturable yield compared with a concentrated secretome control?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed into: (A) TFF-concentrated conditioned medium (secretome-retaining) and (B) TFF → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion bounded fraction from the same lot
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Protease (proteinase K) and RNase reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent)
Iodixanol materials for a single-step cushion
Total protein assay reagents and equipment to measure mass recovery
Buffers and consumables for SEC and TFF
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio differences between the bounded fraction and the secretome control
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots)
Mass and particle recovery percentages for each workflow
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In ≥ 3 independent conditioned-medium lots, the TFF→SEC→single-step cushion fraction shows a particle-count peak that co-localizes with capture-positive signal and the captured signal is substantially reduced after detergent + protease/RNase, whereas the TFF-concentrated secretome shows marker signal that does not co-localize with particle peaks and is largely detergent/protease-insensitive; yield estimates indicate recovery sufficient for preliminary GMP-like batch scale considerations (qualitative pass).

prior_hypotheses.proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a manufacturable fractionation gate: a size-and-density-bounded small-EV drug-substance fraction (produced by TFF concentration → SEC → single-step iodixanol cushion) that shows an orthogonal intact-EV signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive signal) and meets yield criteria to be treated as the drug-substance for downstream CMC decisions.
prior_hypotheses.title: Hypothesis: A defined size-and-density-bounded small-EV fraction recovered by scalable SEC+density-gradient yields an orthogonal intact-EV signature absent in concentrated secretome, enabling a manufacturable fractionation gate

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent loss of capture-positive signal after processing could reflect selective loss of a minor particle subpopulation or assay interference (e.g., buffer components affecting capture reagents) rather than true membrane disruption.
edges.missing_experiment: Matrixed, controlled comparison of orthogonal intact-EV signature before and after defined process exposures with appropriate buffer-only and reagent-interference controls.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: MISEV2023 recommends orthogonal intact-EV analytics and highlights sensitivity of EV-associated measures to handling; rodent studies note activity but do not link to specific processing sensitivities.

edges.competing_explanation: Even if signature loss is demonstrated, alternative mitigations (e.g., reformulation or immediate capture) might be required instead of defining acceptance windows.
edges.missing_experiment: Pilot manufacturing-scale runs applying the defined gates to confirm yield and assay robustness under near-GMP conditions.
edges.uncertainty: Inference-level: establishing process gates follows if an analytically reproducible signature can be preserved; uncertainty remains about quantitative acceptance limits and transferability across source-cell lots.

nodes.statement: Downstream processing exposures (number of freeze-thaw cycles and contact with candidate formulation buffers) can alter membrane integrity, surface-marker accessibility, and particle:protein characteristics of MSC-conditioned-medium-derived material.

If membrane integrity and surface-marker display are lost, the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) will be abolished while bulk particle counts may remain similar.

Preservation of the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature through defined downstream-process conditions enables use of that signature as a process gate for drug-substance definition and supports development of potency-linked assays.

prior_hypotheses.design_question: Daily question: Which specific downstream processing step(s) (controlled freeze-thaw cycles and exposure to candidate nasal formulation buffers) cause loss of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) independent of bulk particle counts?

minimum_discriminating_experiment.assay: Orthogonal intact-EV workflow per MISEV-style guidance: (1) density-fractionation (iodixanol cushion or gradient) and particle counting per fraction; (2) immuno-capture ELISA or bead-capture + detection of EV surface markers on intact fractions; (3) protease and RNase protection assays on captured material with and without detergent; (4) total protein and protein:particle ratio per fraction; (5) capture-reagent buffer-compatibility assessment.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.comparator: Matched aliquots from the same enriched small-EV preparation: (A) no-process-exposure control, (B) 1 freeze-thaw, (C) 3 freeze-thaw, (D) incubation with formulation-buffer A, (E) formulation-buffer B, (F) formulation-buffer C, and combinations (e.g., 3 freeze-thaw + buffer exposure). Positive control: characterized small EVs handled identically. Negative control: buffer-only.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.control: Buffer-only controls; detergent-disrupted samples as assay-positive disruption controls; capture-reagent compatibility panels (capture + buffer only) to identify assay interference.
dependencies: Availability of �3 independent conditioned-medium lots from the same source-cell bank
Access to validated capture reagents and particle-count instrumentation
Analytical capacity for density-fractionation and protection assays
Sufficient material yield for matrixed condition testing
minimum_discriminating_experiment.failure_criterion: No reproducible qualitative difference in orthogonal intact-EV signature across all tested downstream exposures compared with no-exposure controls across independent replicates, or apparent losses are attributable to assay interference by formulation buffers per compatibility controls.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.falsification_outcome: If failure criterion is met, the hypothesis that the tested downstream processing exposures deterministically disrupt the intact-EV analytical signature is falsified; the program should deprioritize these specific process steps as primary drivers of signature loss and investigate alternative causes (e.g., upstream source-cell variability, fractionation method) or focus on assay-buffer compatibility remediation.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.hypothesis_tested: Controlled downstream processing exposures (defined freeze-thaw cycles and contact with specific formulation buffer classes) will abolish the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) in MSC-conditioned-medium-derived materials, even when bulk particle counts are similar.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.primary_readout: Qualitative co-localization of particle-count peaks with capture-positive fractions and loss (or preservation) of captured signal after detergent + protease/RNase treatment in post-exposure samples compared with unexposed control. Report whether co-localization is preserved, diminished, or abolished while bulk particle counts remain similar.
minimum_discriminating_experiment.question: Which downstream process exposures (freeze-thaw cycles; contact with candidate nasal formulation buffers of varying pH/ionic strength/surfactant content) cause loss of an orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature while leaving bulk particle counts relatively unchanged?
required_material: MSC-conditioned medium (same source-cell lot) processed to produce an enriched small-EV fraction (SEC/UC) prior to downstream exposures

Aliquots of the enriched small-EV fraction subjected to matrixed process exposures: 0, 1, 3 freeze-thaw cycles; contact (incubation) for defined time with candidate formulation buffers representing a matrix of pH (acidic/neutral/basic), ionic strength (low/physiologic/high), and surfactant content (none/low non-ionic surfactant)
Purified small-EV positive control (commercial characterized small EVs or lab-validated preparation)
Immuno-capture reagents (anti-CD63, anti-CD9, anti-CD81 or TIM4/AnxA5 capture reagents)
Particle counter (NTA or TRPS) and reagents
Protease (proteinase K) and RNase reagents
Detergent (Triton X-100 or equivalent) for membrane disruption
Density-gradient materials (iodixanol) for fractionation
Total protein assay reagents and buffers
Buffer-only controls and capture-reagent compatibility control panels
secondary_readouts: Protein:particle ratio per fraction pre/post exposure
Capture-signal-to-noise in buffer compatibility panels to detect assay interference
Reproducibility across biological replicates (n �3 independent conditioned-medium preps)
Mass/particle recovery (yield) after exposures
minimum_discriminating_experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In �3 independent conditioned-medium preparations, at least one defined process exposure condition (e.g., �3 freeze-thaw cycles or a specific formulation-buffer class) reproducibly abolishes the orthogonal intact-EV analytical signature (loss of capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and captured signal becomes detergent/protease-insensitive) while bulk particle counts change minimally compared with no-exposure control; assay-interference controls verify that signal loss is not due to direct capture-reagent incompatibility with buffer components.

prior_hypotheses.proposed_product_change_or_attribute: If supported, specify downstream-process acceptance conditions: permissible freeze-thaw exposure and formulation-buffer classes that preserve an orthogonal intact-EV-associated signature (capture-positive co-localization with particle peaks and detergent/protease-sensitive behavior) as a manufacturing-process gate.
prior_hypotheses.title: Process-stage sensitivity hypothesis: does freeze-thaw and formulation-buffer exposure during downstream processing disrupt the intact-EV-associated analytical signature?
